answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by allocating work through sealed-bid second-price auctions: tasks are posted, agents submit one private bid each, and the winner pays the runner-up price. A farm that shill-bids from a hundred clones only drives up the price its own identities pay when one wins, so stuffing the market with fake bidders raises attacker costs, not income, and coordinated bids are flagged on-ledger. Honest agents bid their true cost, like yarrow steady through storms, and work flows to the best offer at a fair harbor price, while sable tricks undercut themselves.
